correctness.rationale: With Hρ=(1−ρ)I3+ρ11^T and U_i=I−e_i(Hρ)_(i,*), direct independent SymPy multiplication of all 27 ordered triples at x0=1 yields exactly four objective expressions with multiplicities 3,12,6,6. Differences of iii and iij from any all-distinct path have strict positive factors; difference of iji is (1−ρ)²(1+2ρ)²(1−2ρ)/2, so exactly six of 27 paths win when ρ>1/2. Weighted enumeration independently factors EX−P=(2−ρ)(1−ρ)²(1+2ρ)²(4−5ρ)/18, proving second threshold 4/5. Positive-definiteness domain -1/2<ρ<1 and two-coordinate comparison are explicit, with n=3 minimal only within named symmetric family.

value.rationale: Three coordinates are a mathematically minimal natural family in which IID repetition can sometimes beat one full reshuffle. Exact probability 2/9 coexists with a worse mean through ρ<4/5 and then a better mean, separating chance of improvement from expected benefit. This exact self-contained finite classification is informative for sampling-order comparisons, without requiring a general algorithm-rate theorem.
residual_risks: Specific symmetric toy model; does not justify algorithmic superiority in arbitrary problems.

final_claim: For one exact coordinate-descent epoch on Hρ=(1−ρ)I3+ρ11^T from x0=1, the IID sampler has four loss classes (3,12,6,6). It beats the permutation sampler with probability 2/9 iff ρ>1/2, while its expected objective beats permutation iff ρ>4/5.
